This game is overhated. I know Randy Pitchford is a sellout, but the work and love the Borderlands dev team has put during the first year can be seen. Performance is now great, I've had a single crash since I started playing, Cash and Loveless are amazing, and overall the game runs great. I couldn't finish BL3 due to its terrible writing, but this game is leagues better in that regard and I find myself chuckling about the stupid jokes often.

I've finished every other BL other than 3, got the Plat on BL2, and I really enjoy BL4. People complain about things like the open world, but to me, this feels the same; technology allows you to have a big single map instead of 4 pieces of a map that need a load screen to move around. The guns lack personality tho, every single one that isn't a pearlscent or a legendary is plain, repetitive and crappy. Music is fine, Borderlands has never been Expedition 33, and the gameplay and gunplay are AMAZING. 

Overall, if you love Borderlands I encourage you to try it and make your own opinion. Fans tend to hate the new thing just enough to drag it until the new one comes, then that one sucks and the previous one "wasn't as bad as people made it to be", and when it comes to BL it has happened to EVERY SINGLE ONE on release after 2, and 2 was a masterpiece for sure, but that doesn't make the other ones bad. Even 2 has a lot of flaws and it's only perfect in a vacuum.

While there have been some improvements in the gameplay, the story/narrative is a complete overreaction to the negative reception of Borderlands 3 and skews too far in the other direction. It takes itself WAY too seriously at times and when there is humour it doesn't land.

However, by far the worst part is the technical state of the game. It has been a full year since release and things have barely improved since launch. I'm actually ok with pre-shader compilation in most instances as I would rather wait a few minutes on first boot than have shader compilation stutter all over the place. The devs of this game have even managed to balls this up: it takes far longer than it reasonably should, still compiles shaders every so often when you load into new areas and STILL manages to have frame drops/stutters regularly. This is not a UE5 problem, this is a problem unique to this game. I've been playing through STALKER 2 recently which also uses UE5 and has a pre-shader compilation on boot, it runs flawlessly. 

I highly doubt that things are ever going to improve, its been a year since launch and not much has changed. Gearbox/2K already have their money, and with the release of the final piece of DLC they have fulfilled their obligation to release content for this game so bar any game breaking issues being fixed the game will probably not receive any further updates at this point.

TLDR: Story is boring, technical state of the game is just as bad as at launch. Stay away.

I honestly don’t understand a lot of the negativity around Borderlands 4. Having played through the previous games, this feels less like the series has “lost its identity” and more like a natural evolution of it. Vault Hunters were never meant to be ordinary people; they are the kind of characters who go up against ridiculous odds, alien horrors, armies and impossible situations and somehow come out the other side. BL4 simply leans further into that.

What I’m enjoying most is how much variety there is. One minute it feels like classic Borderlands, the next I’m wandering into environments that remind me of Alien, Dead Space, Prey, Event Horizon or System Shock. The world actually rewards curiosity, and I’ve repeatedly found myself wandering off the main path just to see what is around the next corner. I don’t see that as Borderlands becoming “generic”, I see it as the universe becoming broader.

The gunplay is excellent, the movement feels great, build experimentation is genuinely fun, and the game constantly gives me reasons to try different weapons and approaches. I’ve also had a very good technical experience so far. On my current PC I’m running the game at very high/max settings and full resolution with frame generation off, and it has been smooth, stable and visually superb.

Is it identical to Borderlands 1, 2 or 3? No, and I don’t think it should be. Those games still exist. For me, BL4 respects what Borderlands was while actually trying to move the series forward. I’m having a blast with it, and I think the developers deserve more credit for the amount of work, imagination and detail that has clearly gone into it. That's my penny's worth against some of these negative reviews.

Free Weekend Review. Great game overall. I finished the main campaign in 15 hours and then as many side quests as I could, which added another 10 hours. I did not expect there to be tons of them, making the main story only the first step.

One thing I miss from the previous games is when selecting a gun from a certain brand, it would shout “GUN GUN GUN!” Now that is gone.

As a looter shooter, having only 4 gun types feels limiting. I did not find many weapon chests, but boss drops were generous, the animation of guns popping out is great. I chose Rafa as my character, he has the abilities of a shoulder mounted cannon, yet I still wanted more firepower, especially since I almost always fight groups of enemies at once. During my first 5 hours, enemies felt mostly limited to bandits and flying enemies, which made me thinking lacking variety. It improves a lot as I continue, and not easy to beat the game solo. Leveling up can be slow, it is difficult to focus only on the main missions because you need side quests to gain levels. I chose the easiest difficulty and still died many times. My best weapon was an SMG fired colorful pigment bullets, with a good chance to generate extra star bullets to hit.

Around half of the mission requires eliminating the enemy in an area. When that was not required, I rushed toward the next area, enemies rarely chased me far. When I needed to clear an area, not every enemy came toward me, so I often had to use the HUD to locate and eliminate the remaining few. This can be helpful because I was not constantly overwhelmed by every enemy at once, but it also makes moving around risky because enemies can be scattered.

The map is huge. I did not unlock every area, there were still many grayed out sections with question marks, the main story only covers around half of the map. Some main story missions require traveling long distances, even with a motorcycle they felt too far away, and I had to keep checking the map for the right route. Clearing safehouses unlocks fast travel points, but there is still a lot of riding. Environments are mostly nice, with interesting trees and remnants of places in Spain, the scenery also changes depending on the time of day. 

The main quests are mostly about combat and skill challenges, while the side quests offer much more. My favorites included creating a music band and watching a short live performance, it has a dark ending where every member is killed because the organizer thinks they are too good. Another good quest is irradiating a seed so it can grow into a tree for poor people; and an escape-room with a maze of breakable walls. The funniest might be helping repair a spaceship and watching it take off, only to see Claptrap carrying a backpack as he tries to get on board. There are other parody missions, such as jumping high and doing a ground slam to cure someone’s back pain; a series of livestream activities that includes sending someone into space using a cannon. There are basic, boring kill missions too, but most of the side quests were enjoyable.

Borderland 4 is currently on 50% off, making a good deal considering the number of quests, the huge maps and all the unlockables. The story is a little silly, the concept reminds me of the first Kingsman movie, with people being controlled through a brain chip. Still, the overall quality is solid. With the new DLC, I would not be surprised if completing all quests takes more than 100 hours.

A good entry to the Borderlands series! It has everything you would expect from a Borderlands game; many of the systems present in previous games were further refined with BL4. 

The big draw for this particular entry are character builds. While I've yet to play the other characters aside from the Gravitar, what I did get to play felt unique and interesting! Like BL3, BL4 gives you the choice between three abilities for each character, but the skill trees are significantly larger and allow for more customization through augments and capstones, which completely change how the ability functions. BL3 also had ability augments, but for the most part, they didn't feel that impactful. The skills and abilities you get access to are also a lot more interesting than BL3! There is a night-and-day difference between BL3's and BL4's character builds, in my opinion. I enjoyed it so much, in fact, that after every major quest I would respec and try a different build.

The game's optimisation leaves a lot to be desired, but you can offset it with frame generation to an extent. For me, it ran at around 60 FPS on ultra graphics with AMD FSR on balanced (at 1440p on a 144hz monitor). After switching to medium graphics, it started running at approximately 100-120 FPS. 

One thing I wish they didn't change from BL3 are side quests. review.review:
I guess it’s my turn to write about how disappointed I was with BL4. Don’t get me wrong - I’ve played every game in the BL series, and I’ve also been playing gacha games for the past two years, so my standards for game quality are so low that you’d have a hard time imagining it. 

However, even by those standards, BL4 managed to be worse than gacha games. I want to point out the elephant in the room: the open world. It’s so open and so vibrant that it offers you all of the following: capturing control points, collecting collectibles, collecting a second type of collectibles, searching for chests, and collecting a third type of collectibles. Even the developers of gacha games are already creating open, vibrant worlds that don’t involve all that hassle. 

Yes, I’ve played about 12 hours of BL4, but even so, I have no reason to go back to the game or load the world, it’s empty and feels like it was procedurally generated. I see a beautiful mountain or a sheer cliff, but I can’t climb it, there’s an invisible wall there. It’s an open world with invisible walls. I want to climb the cliff to explore it, but I can’t, my character can’t climb, and the developer didn’t place any grappling hook points there. It’s an open world with no vertical movement!

What about the characters? Well, each one has 3 × 3 = 9 skill trees, does that add anything? No. It makes no sense if only one branch is actually playable. The player has too many choices - more than they can handle. Same goes for weapons, why do I need a gazillion weapon variants? The weapons now look like a jumble of incomprehensible parts. I no longer enjoy the way the weapons look, it’s all blended into one big mess. Speaking for myself, more ≠ better. 

What about other aspects of the game? The sound is good; the shooting is excellent, the best in the series; the story is good and interesting; the world design is boring to me, but that’s subjective.
So it turns out you have “a premium game made for premium gamers” without a soul, what’s the point of the best shooting system, cutting-edge technology, and a gazillion weapon variations if the world and the game itself are empty, if there’s no reason to return to Kairos? It’s premium candy wrappers for candy whose flavor they forgot to make.

Who might enjoy this game? As I understand it, most of the people who like BL4 are players who discovered the series after BL3 came out. If you're a new player, you'll enjoy the game. But if you're a longtime fan who played BL1, BL2, or BL:TPS, you're better off not spending your money on this - it doesn't have what you're looking for.

Oh, right, also there's no optimization, and the system requirements are way too high.

Something the Borderlands franchise does really well, but that people don’t talk about nearly enough, is its lore and world-building.

And this one in particular is VERY politically charged, especially when you consider the current social and political atmosphere in the real world. I don’t want to get into anything that breaks the rules or guidelines here, but the metaphor is pretty hard to miss: the Timekeepers’ oppressive rule, people being trapped on a planet where they’re essentially being slaughtered, and the way power is maintained through control and fear all hit differently right now.

I don’t want to make everything political, because at the end of the day this is an incredibly fun game. You’re shooting things, looting, laughing at dialogues etc.

But it’s also VERY political, and I think that’s part of what makes the world-building so interesting.

It’s a genuinely very good game, and considering how much people have been sh&&&ing on it since release,

 I don't get why...

But you should get the game

As someone who's played through each of the previous four main titles, several times, I enjoyed this.
I don't care about most of the creative or writing decisions which have moved a great many folks to leave, inspired, reviews.
During the freeplay weekend, I came away from the slightly under sixteen hours of playtime (yes, shaders are a thing [~15 minutes the first go, and another 7 after I recalibrated the screen when I couldn't see any detail in a dark area, and it had to recompile, each time]), and generally had a positive experience.
As shown in the attached spec sheet, I'm using an older CPU, which appear to be largely responsible for the issues that I experienced.  There was CPU bottle-necking, which lent itself to the occasional chop, or laggy performance, but it wasn't anything that I felt was ruining the experience.

Yes, optimization, as most folks are saying, is an issue.  While I never had the pleasure of falling through the floor and having to respawn, I did see a great deal of npc melting into surrounding surfaces, and enemies blinking in and out of existence.  Light flutter at times was distracting - sometimes while I was facing a bright object like vending machines, or in the world with shadows from tree canopies.
I nearly forgot.  Every time I would fast travel, I would get stuck -in- the floor.  I could usually break free by interacting with something nearby like a vending machine.  Sometimes it would just fix itself, and I would just pop up/out.

So, there's a CL4P-TP slider for, what seems to be more of an annoyingly loud robot, than the just ridiculous, delusional, annoying service bot that I've come to know and tolerate.  Great.  Now, can we have a slider for the _speed_ of the eye-wateringly long, un-skippable dialog from the npcs?  I don't need a mandatory life story for characters that are supposed to be substantive in this game.  Character X can just be the way that they are, because they were written that way.  That's all.  Origin stories are not necessary for everyone.

Those are my two main gripes, but I would be remiss if I didn't mention the inventory.

The way that the inventory is arranged now, to me, seems more similar to the way that Tiny Tina's Wonderlands was organized.  It's just different enough for me to have to spend some time to figure out.  Using a large monitor, I shouldn't have to give anything more than a passing glance at an icon or symbol to know what it's supposed to mean, but, for example, the sniper rifle and assault rifle icons are irritatingly similar.  I grew to love the simplicity in design and function that the BL franchise had come to settle on.  Why this needed an overhaul is anyone's guess.  I guess that while that is a bit of a pain, a _real_ quality of life upgrade to me, would be if the developers added a function that that they pushed onto BL3, which was being able to auto-sell user-specified tiered equipment.  Great for inventory management, great for getting cash.

The open world environment is a nice change, but I would prefer a few more fast travel stations.  Say, maybe integrate that feature into each respawn point, and I'd be happy,  As it stands, I spent far too much time in-game trying to get from A to B - and I wasn't even on one of the forgettable fetch-quests!

Yeah, some of the new characters are a bit bland, but as long as I can turn a bullet-hose on bad guys more than sit through boring dialog, I'll be ok.

I'd give it a B, B-

So I decided to install this over the free weekend, fully expecting to absolutely hate it (based on all the bad reviews).

I've been playing BL since part 1, loved 2 and the DLC, loved 3's gameplay changes (but hated the story) and I must say, 4 is better than I thought. A great game? Not sure.
------------------
First, let me tackle the graphics - Hopefully you can see my specs, but I'm having literally no issue playing the game. None. Zero. I'm playing on a 3440 x 1440, I use FSR quality, and I'm getting 80 FPS without framegen. 

Do note: I'm on Fedora Linux, not Windows (sorry, not going back to MS!) and I'm using a 9070XT, not Nvidia.

Most of my settings are maxed or on high and I don't have ANY of the problems everyone else is talking about - no compiling shaders, no lockups, nothing. 

So realize my thoughts on this game are based on that performance. It runs just great.

-----------------
Story - Honestly, the story is so boring I literally don't pay attention to it. The main bad guy is so generic and so lame (so far). His minions really aren't that memorable either.

It's like Gearbox took the flak (haha) for making lots of poop jokes in BL 3 and went ENTIRELY the opposite way. Now it's just "I'm a bad dude and I want to rule or something" yadda yadda yadda.

Honestly, they need some Gen X writers. Seriously. The people they have writing now do some lame crap...then Claptrap literally gets sentimental on a side-quest, more lame crap. I dunno, writing is bad so far. Maybe it improves.
----------------

Gameplay - this really surprised me. I love the double-jump. I already know if I go replay some of the older BLs, I'm going to HATE not having double jump.

Grappling hook - meh. It DOES mean levels can be more vertically-oriented, but honestly I think that slows down the pacing. Not sure I like how vertical some of the stuff is.

-----------------
Talents -- It seems like every Talent has like 3-5 features to it, so you really have to get into your number theory. Are they FUN? I dunno - I played the guy with the two shoulder guns (I literally remembrer zero characters) and it's okay I guess. Tried a couple of other characters.

---------------
Enemies - They seem pretty repetitive, but I do like that at literally level 1, you're already dealing with machines having shields and then metal (two HP bars) - it's like they figured out we know what that is, so you don't have to wait until New Game+ to start dealing with more advanced tactics.

---------------
Design - I'm not really sure about the overworld yet.  What I *DO* like -- the random boss fights (in these small domes) that are challenging (I'm playing on Medium). Discovering little areas sometimes.

What I DON'T like -- much of the overworld is just empty. I hate how your glider controls - very floaty and disconnected, even worse than earlier BL vehicles.

_------------- Overall

I'm not sure, I guess I would hesitantly recommend it if you don't have problems running it and you can get a good price for it.

But as it turns out, there is so much more to that.

"Damn, I should update Windows 10 from version 2004 to 22H2 to play this hilarious game!" And so I made an attempt. But Michael Soft's Mr. Gates wouldn't have that. Over even more hours, no matter what I did, even offline installers, it didn't make this awesome better-than-CachyOS operating system start updating to the best most latest Copilot-enabled version of blessed Windows 10.
But I believed in myself and, more importantly, believed in Randy.
The culmination of a now entire day's worth of research presented a radical solution to update to 22H2, and so I backed up everything I love and hold dear but love not as much as Borderlands; I would name my first child Borderlands. If this broke my install, even more time to play on this holy free weekend would be burned away, but it was the only possible way forward. I did it for you, Gearbox, I did it all for you.

I love diatribes, especially when each instance of one in a quest is essentially the same. I really, truly, enjoyed my regrettably short time playing this game, and if the game was five dollars, I might buy it. Borderlands 4 met my expectations.
After having been put through all those trials, I admit that it is the greatest trick that magician has ever done.

Borderlands 4 is a triumphant return to form that successfully steers the franchise into a more mature era. Gearbox Software clearly listened to the fan feedback from the previous entry, resulting in a game that feels grounded without losing its identity.

Exceptional Gunplay: The absolute star of the show is the combat. The gunplay is tighter, punchier, and more chaotic than ever before. Combined with an overhauled movement system—featuring grappling hooks, dashes, and verticality—engagements feel incredibly fluid and aggressive. The loop of shooting and looting remains brilliantly addictive.

A Grounded, Mature 
Story: Narratively, the game is noticeably more serious than Borderlands 3. It ditches the grating, streamer-centric humor of its predecessor in favour of a more restrained, narrative-driven dystopian setting. While it keeps a healthy dose of classic Borderlands eccentricity, the stakes feel real, and the writing is far better paced.

Performance Visual Tax: The biggest caveat at launch is that technical performance could be an issue for some people. Players running mid-tier hardware may encounter frame drops, stuttering during heavy combat, and optimization quirks. It demands a lot from your hardware, meaning a few settings tweaks might be necessary to get a smooth experience. 

Final Verdict: If you can look past the current technical rough edges, Borderlands 4 delivers exactly what fans wanted: a refined, thoughtful, and action-packed evolution that proves there is still plenty of life left in this iconic looter-shooter franchise.

I beat the entire game over the free weekend on the idea that if I came away really enjoying it, I would buy the game and DLC to continue with it. As an avid enjoyer of all previous Borderlands games (yes, that includes 3), this game is simply underwhelming, if not bad.

For statistics purposes: 27 hours of playtime. I played on Hard difficulty as Vex and reached level 44 by the time I stopped. I used a Trouble crit build for about 65% of my playthrough before switching to an Eldritch Blast HP tank build for the remainder. I opened and defeated 1 of the 3(?) Vaults in the open world, completed all of the Auger faction side quests, finished both the Airship and Goredello world events, and completed a good chunk of the open-world objectives. I also farmed 2 bosses for their legendary drops for fun, without knowing what they dropped. I ended with 14 legendaries, 2 pearlescents, and 143 unopened loot crates in my inventory. Oops.

The actual gameplay is pretty good. The shooting feels great, and the new movement abilities are a big step forward for the series imo. The double jump and dash feel amazing. I just wish the grappling hook wasn't so limited. The side quests that I played were also great. I really liked the new characters introduced, and the returning characters felt like they were done justice, particularly Claptrap.

Moxxi's Encore machines are an incredible idea that I'm surprised it took them until this entry to figure out lol. My only issue is that I wish you could fast travel directly to them to begin farming. The main boss fights are also quite good. I enjoyed all of them, although I was less impressed by the open-world bosses. My favourite open-world boss was the Battle Wagon. It was completely unexpected and cool enough that it became one of the bosses I farmed. I also really like the random enemy modifiers. They aren't crazy enough to change your entire game plan and are simple enough to interpret on sight. They add good variety to the general combat.

While these are all great things, just about everything else is either plain middling or straight-up bad.

The music stinks. Not much to say other than that. I don't know why they did not bring back Jesper Kyd for Borderlands 4. He did an excellent job on every other game.

The game is also very annoying about you not owning the DLC. This may have been the same with Borderlands 3, but I wouldn't know. There are hub areas where characters yell at you about how you've gotta do their epic DLC mission every time you go there. It gets annoying quickly.

I experienced several minor bugs throughout the game. NPC pathing broke several times. Gates and doors would be open but have an invisible wall in their place. Enemies would stand still and let me kill them in a "my animations are broken" kind of way. Bounty targets wouldn't spawn. Quest dialogue would skip itself or play out of order.

There's also a part where [spoiler]you go to the moon Elpis, and there are Rippers there, and I hate it. The Ripper Queen section of the game is about how Callis wants to go to the moon because of her prophecy, and you prevent her from doing this. But when you get there, the Rippers are already there with a bunch of bases set up.

They explain that it was a scouting party sent there preemptively, but that kind of defeats the whole crazy plot of trying to build a rocket platform to the moon lol. I think they should have instead introduced a small Guardian faction like the ones from The Pre-Sequel, or reskinned some bandits as Skavs, also from The Pre-Sequel.[/spoiler] This part just really bothers me.

Then there's the main story. The Timekeeper is an incompetent moron. Not only is he barely present through most of the story, he barely ever uses his powers. The first time he meaningfully uses them, during the opening, is a cool moment. It establishes how powerful he is and why we should fear him. But the second time he does so creates a stupid plot hole that ruins everything.

[spoiler]The cutscene where Zadra dies is awful. She acknowledges how the Timekeeper targeted ECHO-4 and doesn't second guess that you could be controlled at all? Not even when it has already been shown that people being controlled by the Timekeeper have glowing yellow eyes?

Later, he takes control of your friends and implies he will kill them if you do not comply. You don't comply, and he doesn't follow through with the threat. He also never tries anything like that again except at the end of the game.[/spoiler] Talk about frustrating.

I understand that if they made the Timekeeper actually smart and competent, it would be difficult to make a full game out of him, but they chose to write his powers this way. [spoiler]There are also several characters who do not have Bolts. In an alternate universe, I could see there being more focus on these characters, maybe trying to figure out how to safely remove people's Bolts or forming an alliance with the Rippers for the climax.

The story itself feels very insular. Nothing that happens seems to have much impact on the overarching story. The only major development I can think of is that they basically undid the ending of Borderlands 3 by bringing Lilith back.[/spoiler] Overall, this entry just feels like kicking the can down the road on the whole war idea introduced in The Pre-Sequel.

Now for the open world.

It suffers from the common trappings of open worlds. It is too big for its own good, with too few fast-travel locations. You spend way too much time driving around just moving from place to place. They removed the minimap, instead opting for a compass system, which makes both gameplay and exploration suffer imo. You constantly have to open the map to see where you need to go or drop a marker. You can then hit Z to have ECHO-4 guide you to your destination.

The ECHO-4 guide is broken. It frequently sends you down inconvenient paths, loops back on itself, or suggests you should phase through walls to reach your destination. Navigation was already boring, but now it is also frustrating.

The game also suffers from classic open-world asset reuse. Emphasis on "suffers," because there is a smart way and a bad way to do this. Borderlands 4 opts for the bad way. There are copy-pasted objectives all over the world that create the illusion of content. The ECHOs are fine. They add some lore and story. The Vault Symbols are classic Borderlands, so I can't knock them too badly. But some of the others suck.

The Deadbolts, as far as I could tell, do not contribute anything other than basically being a reskinned Vault Symbol/ECHO with no lore. The Vault Hunter Guides are kind of a reused version of the Typhon DeLeon audio logs from Borderlands 3, but this time featuring Arjay. They expand on the world a little, but aren't all that interesting. There are statues where you need to find and collect 3 connected orbs. They also provide some lore, but the only real difference from the Arjay logs or ECHOs is that you have to find 4 things to obtain it. There are also safes and shrines that grant you loot.

Then there are the stupid data caches. These are the worst. You have to find them and carry them back to a safe house to collect them. Here's this big open world designed around having a vehicle to help you get around quickly, and here's an objective where you can't use your vehicle. You gotta walk it, buddy. Really bad.

There are also giant machines where you need to find a battery to activate them and then climb to the top to get the thing inside. These are a little more interesting at least. Another open-world objective is the propaganda stations, where you let ECHO-4 hack the station while you kill enemies. These are normally a lot of fun, but out of the 10 or so that I did, about half had issues with enemies not spawning or hiding far away and not coming towards me, preventing the hacking from progressing.

TL;DR it's worth <= 35, new hunters are fine, cosmetic packs are pointless and underwhelming.

So like a bunch of other people, I loved BL1 when it was new, and was pretty fond of BL2. Pre-sequel and 3 never got my attention, I honestly don't even think I played it, and I just stopped paying attention after that. I hopped on here because I didn't realize 4 was even out, and the free weekend seemed like a good chance to kill some time.

That being said, this game is in NO WAY as bad as everyone else is saying it is. It's definitely Borderlands, and it's still top of it's class in looter-shooters. The movement feels great(*), the gunplay and gun variety is awesome, there's a ton of build variety with the augments (it just gives you + talent points, even if you don't have any slotted, so you could just get something stupid like +50% fire damage, +200% sniper damage, and 25% magazine replenish on weapon swap from a single gear slot) and there's enough stuff going on in the map to the point where it doesn't feel like you're traveling for 5 minutes just to do some throwaway quest.

That being said, ♥♥♥♥ no it's not worth 60 bucks. The story is *fine*, the humor isn't great, and there's still bugs. None of which are game-breaking, but they still exist and are likely to happen(*). The humor might just be me not being the target demographic anymore, considering I thought BL1 was funny almost 20 years ago, but most of the jokes just fall flat with me. The story itself is pretty decent, and the characters are endearing-ish, but you can smell the jokes coming from a mile away. E.G; rest assured, if someone says "I'm so happy I could kiss you!", just know that there WILL be a direct follow-up line of "Only if you're into it, I mean" or "I mean, hypothetically, of course, you're not really my type. Unless...?" because that joke has happened four times already, with at least 4-5 other "sex funny" jokes sprinkled in just as effectively. Outside of the jokes though, the characters have good voice actors and decent lines, which is really all you can ask for when it comes to campy action games like this.

The stuff that isn't broken(*) hasn't been fixed, so the guns and shields and stuff all do interesting things, I haven't seen all of the manufacturers yet so I don't know how many there are exactly, but out of the 6-7 that I've seen, they all function fundamentally differently outside of shooting projectiles, and they can have bits from other manufacturers added to them. (E.G; Torgue AR with a Maliwan part that makes the rockets elemental, or an Order SMG with a Ripper part that turns an otherwise charge-to-burst gun into a spool-up, ~0 recoil, pinpoint accurate fully automatic). Guns good.

The bugs are prevalent though, that's kind of inexcusable at this point. There's a pretty sizable amount of issues from what appears to be game state management, from what I've seen. There's trucks that need to have batteries damaged, so you can get to the chest that's in them, and I have not once been able to access the chest in the back, because after breaking the batteries, the game does not seem to register the batteries as broken. I've also had the same issue twice, where a boss that goes underground and re-emerges will stop taking damage when they come above ground, I assume because they are still being viewed as "below ground". Pair that with the fact that occasionally, and in one instance resulting in a death, the ground will just decide to not load its hitboxes (resulting in you falling straight through the floor, which killed me once and confused me 4-5 times), and you have the entire reason why I'm saying this game is in no way worth the full ticket price. 

Long story short, the bugs are there but only really screwed me up twice, but otherwise it's fun. If you actually like Borderlands you'll like it, if you think that this is going to re-ignite the nostalgia and be a modern-day re-experiencing of BL1, just buy BL1 for like 3 dollars on GOG.

I really hate having to give a Borderlands game a thumbs-down, but in this case, I have to.

As background, I _love_ the Borderlands franchise.  Let's face it, BL2 is an absolute masterpiece, and I'll flat out say that I think Handsome Jack is the single best villain in video game history, period.  BL1, the pre-sequel, and BL3 didn't quite achieve the perfection that was BL2, but all of them were very good games filled with humor, heart, excitement, and variety.  Unfortunately, BL4 seemingly has none of those things.

Full disclosure, I have not played the game all the way through.  I picked it up during this free play weekend, figuring that was a great way to give it a try.  So I've played about 12 hours/20% of the main campaign (though my steam playtime says 15 hours because I spent 2-3 hours compiling shaders and figuring out linux compatibility grrr...).  Proton Experimental, btw, for any other linux players out there.

Anyway, The gameplay is fine, actually pretty good, but the characters, especially the villains, are bland, soulless, and, the worst sin of all in a Borderlands game, humorless. I wasn't especially enamored of the twins in BL3, but at least they were entertaining at times.  

Also, they moved to an open world design, which I don't think does the game any favors.  Rather than unique landscapes and carefully crafted levels, you kind of have a mishmash of stuff all over the place.  Now I can understand why they did it - I can see the intent behind it and I think it was genuinely well-intentioned.  You move from region to region, and you capture waypoints, which open fast travel stations in those regions, so as the game progresses you kind of open up the world and clear out the fog of war.  It's a neat idea.  But it just sacrifices too much flavor in the process.

But the game's not a complete disaster... I've actually gotten into the story, and I'm kind of curious how it plays out.  And I did enjoy playing Vex - maybe the first time I've really enjoyed playing a "pet" class in anything.  Just not enough to pay the exorbitant price tag.

I'll probably keep it on my wishlist just so that I'm notified of any sales.  If they come out with a GOTY edition with all the DLC included and I can get that in a bundle or for around $15, I'd consider it.

I'm probably making it sound worse than it is...  it's really not awful.  It's just very mediocre, and probably appears worse by way of comparison with what came before.  I wish I could give it a thumb-sideways review. Having played and enjoyed every Borderlands game (except 3), when I saw there was a Free to Play weekend, I thought it would be interesting to try this game.

TLDR; This game is what I expected it was before I even played it, feels like everything except a Borderlands game, none of that Borderlands charm is there, or very little of it is. However, the gunplay and movement are definitely things I enjoyed in this game, and despite the game lacking in many ways from previous installments, it ultimately is a fun game to play, however it should have just been its own game, instead of being a Borderlands game as it feels like the developers wanted to make something other than Borderlands.

For those curious in my full thoughts.

When I first saw this game, my instant thought was, "this looks nothing like Borderlands." After playing through most of the game, that thought has only just felt more true. Absolutely nothing about this game feels like Borderlands, in fact, quite the opposite. It feels like I am playing everything but Borderlands, outside of the few Borderlands things sprinkled in to remind me that I am. (i.e characters mainly, Claptrap, Moxxi, Lilith.) The style, the aesthetic, and the design that went behind every single aspect of BL1, 2, and TPS that made those games so great and feel so unique and memorable, everything from environments, to art style and aesthetic, to world locations, characters and story, down to tiny things like music, humor, or even animations that gave those games that unique charm is just missing significantly in this game if not outright absent. 

This game kinda feels like a mishmashed amalgamation of every sci-fi IP; Destiny, Warframe, hell even some Cyberpunk aspects, everything except for Borderlands. Honestly, if someone let me play this game and I didn't know what it was, I wouldn't immediately recognize it as Borderlands unlike the other games. It kinda feels like the developers really wanted to make something other than Borderlands but unfortunately had to make another installment for this franchise. In my opinion, they should have just made this into its own thing. On its own, isolated from the franchise, this game is actually fairly decent and I had fun playing it, but having the prior expectations set by the standards of the previous games, this game doesn't really hold up well.

The best thing about this game is the gunplay in my opinion. They feel smooth and satisfying to use, they have oomf, they sound incredible, and are genuinely fun, especially with the alternative fire modes for most of them, and the models look really good, even though the aesthetic of the manufacturers is a bit messed up with how they tried to make them all look even more sci-fi. Additionally, the new movement tech in this game is also really fun, taking the parts from TPS that I loved, double jumping and ground slamming, but also adding dodging, sliding, and now a grappling hook, make traversing and combat even more fun, so that is a positive for me.

The world in this game is ok, even though it really isn't well optimized, it is beautiful, even on the lower settings I had to run it, and there are interesting locations that if this game was its own thing, would be enough, but unfortunately, because it is a Borderlands game, it doesn't quite capture that same memorability and intrigue that made the well crafted environments from past games feel so unique. The enemies aren't really as interesting as they are in the past games as well. I find some of the enemies quips to be more annoying here honestly, where as in BL2, I love constantly quoting them because of how stupidly vulgar or silly they can sound. That and they were interesting to fight against, they kinda felt like a character in their own right and not just a target to shoot at. The story and the characters in this game are...ok, if this game was it's own thing, it would be a decent, passable story, but because its a Borderlands game, the bar is set incredibly high from the past games, and this game is no where close to meeting it. Humor in this game feels really forced, some of the lines got me, but most of it is outright annoying, if not just completely forced.

However, despite the negative thoughts that I have on this game, I do still think it is a fun game although I REALLY feel like it should have just been its own thing. If I am paying money for a Borderlands game, I am gonna expect a Borderlands experience, and this game fails ALOT of those expectations spectacularly, but it is still fun. I definitely wouldn't pick this up at full price, if I had the chance, I would at a steep discount, because I did enjoy the gameplay for the most part. It is honestly good enough that personally I could ignore all of the other issues with the game if I just wanted something fun to play, but if I wanted to play a Borderlands game, I'm not finding it here. If it is something that you enjoy, great, I can see some of the reasons why you might, however, if I wanted a Borderlands experience, I am better sticking with BL1, BL2, or TPS. I can't really recommend it to people interested in Borderlands, but I can recommend it to people who just want something fun to play. (Even though I would also encourage playing the older games, because those games are more incredibly fun experiences themselves.)

Overall, Borderlands 4 isn't... bad. But it doesn't wow me either.
Before I get to the main bulk of my critique, I will quickly state that the game seems to have a problem when it comes to compiling shaders at the moment. Takes a fair few minutes, even with an AMD Ryzen 9 9900X and an RTX 5080. I imagine with lower-end specs, compiling shaders will take even longer. 

And the game will compile shaders at least twice before you're able to actually play: one time when launching the game, the second time when loading up a character file.
The game also seems to have the tendency to crash whenever you try alt-tabbing to another window. With that out of the way, my main critique of the game has to do with arguably the most important aspect of the game: the guns.

It's clear that Gearbox has tried renovating the guns of the game once again. A couple gun brands I found myself enjoying such as Jakobs and Vladof. Torgue is alright. Every other gun brand however feels significantly underpowered to me. On top of that, something about the weapon designs for many gun brands have lost their special unique touch. Only Jakobs feels like it stands out, retaining its old western aesthetic, but even it has some generic sci-fi scopes attached to it. And really many of the other gun brands look like each other to much extent.
These factors together have led me to relying on only a few gun brands with one Shock gun intended to shred shields, which really becomes pretty boring in the long run. Borderlands should be all about experimenting and mixing it up with your weapon loadouts, but with how most gun brands are in BL4, only a few stand out as reliable. With the gunplay getting boring, I don't find myself enjoying BL4 in the long run. The premise of the story doesn't wow me either. Villain feels like a way more boring version of Handsome Jack.

Speaking of him, I do recommend giving Borderlands 2 a shot. I do feel that BL2 was the last great Borderlands game and it has a pretty nice story. To this day, people still talk about how amazingly written the villain is, and I do think it has aged rather well.

I wish there was a way to do a "mixed" review, or a way to review with a caveat. 

DISCLAIMER - THIS IS A FREE WEEKEND REVIEW DURING THE FREE WEEKEND OF 9/11/26-9/14/26. I AM A BORDERLANDS OLDHEAD, and WAS WAITING FOR SOMETHING LIKE THIS TO TEST THE GAME WITH.

Bottom Line Up Front: Its solid. 
Its not as good as 3 or 2, but its solid. Pick up on sale for 50% or more. As of writing, it is $30 USD for the base game and $64.99 for the super deluxe edition including all of the DLCS.  

It seems that the game is in a better spot than it was when it launched a year ago, and now the latest DLC and new character were very good and steps in the right direction. 

Perhaps give it more time to cook and a better discount.

Long version -
I am a borderlands oldhead. My first borderlands save I have on any device I own is from November 2009. So yeah. been playing this series a really long time.  

This is the first, and only Borderlands game I did not preorder, or get on launch. Yes. Im serious. I even got the original way back when. Little elementary school me.

I see what they were going for. I can say they overcorrected in several respects. They wanted to address Borderlands 3's toilet humor and unseriousness as well as BL3's planets and maps. They wanted to keep it more grounded with a more serious story that plays it straight. They also went with a open world on one planet to try and provide more depth. 

Hers the problem. The story ends up bland, and not even feeling very borderlandsy at times, and the open world is basically an assassins creed game where the side content feels like an aimless checklist semi-often.

Some of the quests and quips have been fun, I have enjoyed Vex so far besides her being a stereotypically edgy alt girl. (It has its benefits and negatives). 

However, THIS IS BORDERLANDS. IT IS A SERIES THAT IS KNOWN FOR ITS DOWNRIGHT STUPID OR OVER-THE-TOP silliness or exaggerated stuff. Here we are playing it serious and its almost bland at times and comes off as "BL3 was too much so lets go borrow from destiny" STOP. I played both Destiny and Borderlands since either game was released. And yes, the first ones. Borderlands was ALWAYS better than Destiny. ALWAYS. Argue with me if you want but Borderlands was never truly dethroned by its competitors. It is still THE SUPREME looter shooter.  So imagine my disappointment when booting the game up and feeling a distinct lack of borderlands until I got in my last like 5 hours of gameplay, which is 20ish hours in, and my character is already level 29.

Gameplay - this is quite good actually. The gunplay, abilities, movement tech, grapple hook, all feels great. No complaints here. The weapons having a lot of alternate fire modes or quirks, also good. I like this. Legendaries are a bit rarer and feel more like the Red-Text unique purples from BL3. IF you know what I mean by that, you know what I mean by that. This front I don't have many complaints on. It is definitely borderlands. Some of the characters are better than others, and I understand that the DLC characters are heads and shoulders above the base game characters. But I did not pay for them as this is a free weekend review.

Story - according to the game I am 44% through the story. Im gonna be honest the first two hours were ROUGH. And judging by other reviews ive seen with only two hours, it bounced a lot of people off, including my friends, who are ALSO big borderlands vets like me. I stuck it out because I knew from watching several reviews already that it does get better. 

The problem is - the characters are mostly bland and forgettable with few exceptions or fun quirks. They play it to serious and try to make you like everyone. Full stop. I do feel the 2nd lieutenant, the Ripper Queen was a more interesting and better antagonist than Sol, but it still is pretty surface level stuff. The side characters are mostly boring. Though the returning characters are nice. LOT OF MODERN HUMOR, for better or worse. Not as abrasive and obnoxious as BL3, but a few challenge names and weapon descriptions made me go "oh for real now? we out here quoting the 2024 memes?" 

I did not finish the story, but so far it did not really hook myself or my friends in a strong way. I have only really felt anything in regards to it now that I have gotten almost halfway through it. 

Gearbox is forever stuck in the shadow of Handsome Jack, and it will be very difficult to emulate that same smash success that he was like that again. BL3, and now BL4 prove that.

TECHNICAL/BUGS:
I will preface. In most games, I very rarely experience bugs. Maybe I am uniquely lucky, but I am not someone who gets crashes, bugs, or glitches often, or at all, really. 

This game is BUGGY. I experienced at least 3 crashes. 2 of which were due to me tabbing out and coming back after a few minutes. There are many times I got stuck on a object, or after fast traveling I couldn't move and had to either re-travel or exit to menu. Plenty of weird latency things, as well as just what felt like weird/awkward controls when trying to compare weapons. 

On a technical level the game has nice quality of life, excellent customization and accessibility features. It also looks very nice visually. Though, it really isn't a huge jump over Borderlands 3, which came out 7 years ago now (I feel so old saying that. I still feel like BL3 is new....) Its mostly shaders, lighting, and VFX that carries 4 over visually.

There are two notable downgrades. I admit they are very big nitpicks and TBH you can disregard it, but I noticed it and it bothered me.  1. Staged reloads are gone. One of my favorite details in BL3 is Jakobs and other weaponry loading the exact amount of bullets you expended or reloaded. Also a weapon animation stopping and remembering where you were in the process if you interrupted it by sprinting or another action. Small details, but it really means a lot.  2. This ones petty.  Meleeing the small cardboard boxes DOES open them like BL3, but they don't go flying. and thats lame.

PEFORMANCE
I am going to be heavily skewed because I have a 5070ti 16gb, ryzen 7 9800x3d processor and 32gb of ram, and I have the game on a 4tb m.2 SSD.  So yeah, it isn't exactly going to be a fair comparison for most people's systems.

WITHOUT frame generation, I was rocking 78-80ish frames, 100ish depending on the environment. For maxed out settings thats good. Until you realize what my rig is, and in reality it should be higher than that. I'm not sure what is such a hog with this game. I turned on Framegen and dlss all of that stuff and then i'm rocking like 200+ frames pretty consistently. So I'm not sure what exactly is going on under the hood that results in the game having such a rough performance, even for people with 40 series cards or more recent cards, but its noteworthy enough I have to mention it, even if I personally didn't have issues with it. I also do believe there have been technical improvements over the last year, as I have read online.

OVERALL TAKEAWAY
I think the game has potential still. Even for some of its faults or core issues that are just a product of design. Right now it is unknown if there will be further DLCs after what just released, as it was one of the last things planned for the 1 year of post-launch content included in the super deluxe edition. It has reviewed quite well. If Gearbox continues with the same level of quality and work with the latest releases on 9/10/26, the game can easily punch its way up because it fundamentally has good gameplay, and it seems they've learned from the base game of BL4.

But I cannot in good faith recommend the game without at least a 50% discount. Either get it now during this sale, or wait until Christmas, or future sales.  $30 for the base game is ok, but the dlcs have to be considered, and that makes it $65.

I may revisit this review in the future, if I can get the game on a above 50% discount, and if things turn around for the game.

It's ok. Honestly, I enjoyed it more than I thought I would, but that might just be because I've seen so much bad stuff about this game that my bar was really, really on the floor.

The Good: 

Gameplay is fun. Characters are great as always, and their abilities feel unique and impactful. This is one of the things borderlands does best. I've been told that some of them fall off and feel underpowered in the endgame but I obviously wasn't able to get there during a free weekend so I can't comment on this other than to say that I enjoyed what I saw.

Writing was actually pretty good, better than what some people have made it out to be. Nothing exceptional but it was at least tolerable and even engaging at some points, which is more than can usually be said for this series. Most of the jokes suck as usual, but a couple were funny. I chuckled a few times. To my shock, the game even seems to know when to be serious and when not to be, a rare thing for a borderlands title. For example, there was an early side quest in which a man's brother was murdered, and the game manages to treat the murder as a serious event rather than something to be quipped about. The entire time I expected the surviving brother to make a stupid cliche joke like "oh well, I hated him anyway," or something, and was astonished when he never did. 

I also didn't hate the open world as much as some do. Some people say it feels empty, but imo it wasn't any worse than Bl2's The Dust or The Pre-Sequel's... everything. Though of course, it doesn't really add anything to the game either, except for a lot of lag and loading times. The design of the actual locations with their enemies and loot is pretty much par for the course if ever so slightly stingier on chests than previous titles.

The Bad: 

Nothing really major but lots of little micro-complaints that add up over time.

First of all, yet the performance is pretty bad. I have a decent rig, not exceptional but the game recommended I play on high settings so I did. However I must emphasize that when people say the game's performance is bad what they really mean is the game is really, really bad about compiling shaders. No doubt these two words strike fear into every bl4 player's heart. When you first start up the game it will take several minutes to compile shaders. For me it was around 2-3 minutes but I've heard for some people it can take 10 or more. then, when you actually load into the world, it will compile shaders a second time, thankfully faster than the first. In theory it will only have to do both of these once, however any time the game updates, and sometimes completely at random, it will have to do this very long process again. Mind you you have not even started playing the game yet. Then, once you're actually in the game, you get the occasional stutter which is more frequent when you are either moving fast in your bike or approaching an area with a lot of objects like a town or enemy base. Do you want to know what's causing that stutter, my friend? Yes, you guessed it. That's the game compiling shaders a third time right before your very eyes.

The UI also has some little micro-issues which add up over time. For example, in Bl2 equipped guns are automatically sorted to the bottom of you inventory so that you won't accidentally sell them. In bl4 they are mixed in among all your other guns, which is a pointless and easily fixable inconvenience. Why is it like this?

There is also no minimap. I recall that before release the developers said that there was a radar, and that this was equivalent but it isn't. You don't use the minimap to find enemies, you use it to find collectable and quest objectives. For instance if there is a quest objective at the top of a tall cliff, you can usually use the minimap to locate a way up the cliff. Here that convenience is pointlessly removed. Again, why?

Another minor but annoying inconvenience is the guns themselves. In previous games all the different gun types had very distinct shapes which made them easy to identify. Here they're all a vaguely sci-fi-ish blob of gun parts which can make it hard to tell them apart. For example it can be hard to tell an assault rifle from an smg because some rifles are short enough to pass as smgs, and some smgs long enough to pass as assault rifles until you hover over them. This is further compounded by the fact that the silhouette of items frequently gets obscured by ground cover like grass. In previous games grass was much more sparse and this was not an issue. Often a boss will drop 4-5 different pieces of loot and I end up having to mouse over every single one to see if any of them would be good for my build, when in previous games I could tell at a glance most of the time.

Also, this one is more subjective but a lot of the lootable chests in this one are quite oddly shaped and smaller than previous games, which can make it somewhat difficult to tell at a glance what is a loot chest vs an ammo chest or junk chest. If it weren't for the series standard green glowy lights on them it would be hard to tell that some objects are even meant to be lootable at all.

Some have complained that the enemies in this game feel too repetitive and same-y. I can definitely see this. I think the bigger problem, though, is that in some cases they spawn and respawn way too frequently. In earlier games, if you cleared out an area it was cleared until you restarted the game, meaning you were free to traverse it for whatever objectives you wanted. Here a cleared out area will be refilled with enemies just a few minutes after you leave, meaning that if you need to pass through multiple times for a quest or even just to grab a collectible you missed there's a good chance that you'll have to kill the exact same enemies again.

On that note there are many such quests which do this. Borderlands quests have never been great but in this one they are especially bad. Go there, kill this, grab that. There is nothing interesting about them. I managed about two or three before I began to lose interest entirely. The rewards are also pretty bad. Some don't even offer you a gun, just Money and Eridium - Eridium which is much less useful than in previous games.

So do I recommend it? Yes, but not right now. Even the current 50% sale it's too expensive, especially since the best content in Borderlands games is always in the DLCs. Put it on your wishlist and in a year or two once it's no longer being patched and the price is down to 75-90% off like bl3 is right now, it'll be well worth the price. But currently? No.

TLDR: I recommend it for what it will be, not for what it currently is.

[b]What I like:[/b]
[list]
[*] FPS gunplay is great.
[*] I like the open world mechanics.  But this does come with caveats.
[/list]

[b]Caveats:[/b]
[list]
[*] Like most open world games, this one is incomplete without a buddy.  This is not nearly as good of a game, played solo.
[*] The best open world games have a lot of variety of locales and sights to see.  In 18 hours of Kairos, the world didn't feel particularly distinct in any way.
[*] There is a lot to do, but there is a real risk that fun turns into work.  I am unconvinced that Gearbox struck that balance, but I played for 18 hours before the free play period ended.
[/list]

[b]Criticism:[/b]
[list]
[*] Borderlands 4 lacks the charm of Borderlands 2.
[*] Borderlands 4 does have a good cast of heroes, but I feel like they lack the style found in Borderlands 2.  Zer0 and Gaige from Borderlands 2 remain my all time favorites.  Although I did have fun playing Vex.
[*] Psychopath CEO, Handsome Jack, was the kind of antagonist that you just love to hate, so his defeat at the end  of Borderlands 2 is very, very satisfying.  I don't feel the same about The Timekeeper.  He's an authoritarian god figure that doesn't stand out in any meaningful way.  But at least The Timekeeper isn't a skin-irritant like the Twins from Borderlands 3.
[/list]

[b]Ugh.[/b]  😖
[list]
[*] Here is another Unreal Engine 5 game demanding a top shelf GPU.  For reference, my Radeon 6700 XT roughly compares with a Geforce RTX 5060 or 4060ti.  On medium settings, my framerate is between 45 - 65.  On low, I can get 60 - 80.  And this is at 1080p, native resolution, no frame generation.  But Borderlands 3 is a full 144 fps at the highest settings.  😓
[*] My partner, who played with me, has a Radeon 7800 XT (roughly comparable to an RTX 4070 or 5060ti), and was able to get 45 - 60 fps at very high settings.  Again, at 1080p.  Certainly better, but still underpowered.
[*] Wait for a big sale.  Because the base game is $70.  💰 Add another $200 for DLC.  💰 And you need a $750 GPU to play it well. 💸
[*] Sure, you don't have to buy the DLC, but you will be repeatedly reminded of what you [i]don't[/i] have as you play.  Here's a quest board with heroic stuff to do...  oh but you don't have the mission pack DLC.  There's the Vault Card in my character screen showing challenges and unlockable content.  Oh, but four of the five cards are locked behind DLC.  😞  Might as well spring for the Super Deluxe pack.  "Only" $130.  🤑
[/list]

[b]Verdict:[/b] 👎
Let me be clear:  This is not a [i]bad[/i] game.  There are good times to be had.  But for what Borderlands 4 demands, this had better not only be Game of the Year, but also Game of the Decade.  It is neither.  It is not even the best Borderlands game.

[h1]We were so close, man[/h1]
Like a lot of people I was scared away from the game due to the price and the egregiously bad performance, but while I can't say the latter has changed (granted, I don't have the greatest GPU these days but a game that runs and scales this bad in a hardware economy like this is awful either way), the game itself, from a feel and gunplay and loot variety perspective, to me feels like the best to date.

I speedran the story to get through the free weekend, had to level grind just a little bit since things can still get  ahead of you. It's fine - inoffensive at worst I'd say, which unfortunately is a huge improvement over 3 but it's still a sign they're aware of how bad that was. There's stakes you can feel, but the antagonists are almost...TOO generically malicious, dark and moustache-twirlingly evil? In a way this was kind of an overcorrection but I'll take it. There are some twists here and there I didn't expect in the best way, so there's that. The very end also just kinda feels like (spoilers here) [spoiler]them finally acknowledging/remembering that The Pre-Sequel exists, that they had a cliffhanger ending talking about a "war that is coming" and saying "don't worry, we didn't forget about this plot thread!" Like, okay, cool, I'm glad you didn't, but also can we PLEASE get to the point soon?[/spoiler]

So, I'm a BL1 truther in that I still felt like with 3, the weapon randomization still wasn't where it needed to be like it was in the original game. The gimmicks that started with 2 did add something to the table, but the lack of interchangeable weapon parts and how rigid every weapon felt kinda let things down and 3 kind of tried to fix that, but not enough. 4 though...my god, 4 has managed to make blues feel exciting again, hell I even look at greens now, because the "cross-licensed parts" system leads to an unbelievable amount of variety and brings back some weapon archetypes that have been dead since 2, like fully auto Torgue gyrojets. Some of the blues and purples you get feel like they'd be legendaries in previous games!

And shooting those guns feels amazing - the enemy variety is a bit too low but they're still fun to fight regardless and the pace is kicked up a notch, and also encourages you to be more mobile like you're playing Doom 2016 or Eternal. The added side/back/air dash and hover is great, the grapple allows for some absurd speed boosts and the feedback of weapons is even better now, with better looking and more excessive blood and gore from each hit and kill. The major bosses are also extremely fun and intense, and even have actual mechanics! BL3 had good bosses too, but man these were great. I love that Gearbox's boss design has evolved sorta into bullet hell territory.

[h1]Bloaterlands 4[/h1]
Really, besides the performance and price, my major and biggest complaint is that the open world is unnecessary, makes the game feel like the General Knoxx DLC on steroids with all the driving, and worst of all: makes the game and world's scope feel smaller than every previous one. There were only 4 real biomes that I saw in my time: green coastline, Pandora-like desert, cold mountains and decaying megacity. It basically boils down to "green, brown, and grey/white" and severely hurts both environment AND enemy variety. The world feels smaller now ironically specifically because of this, and while there are still cool setpieces, dungeons and vistas, you just don't get the same feeling Borderlands 2 gave of seeing everything Pandora had to offer. Kairos feels really one-note as a result - enemies barely change between each region, you'll still be fighting the same Rippers and Order synths and the fauna doesn't change much either.

And I do want to say something about the performance: it doesn't feel like the game looks like it justifies it. The game relies on RAGE levels of texture streaming with your guns loading them in even between swaps, and Lumen...oh my god, Lumen, I hate it, I hate it so much. The game basically has forced RT at all times through it which causes so many problems: garbage performance (again), grainy shadows, ghosting, patches of light bleeding/artifacting through the grain especially when transitioning from exteriors to interiors, hell the game takes like several minutes to register when it's night and the lighting should change so night looks way too bright for some reason until it fixes itself. The game is also so egregiously bloated at 173GB that it would make a modern Call of Duty blush. UE5 is the engine from hell, and it's MURDERING this game's artistic direction with its issues.

All in all I would say this would be a mostly-good game on it's current sale price as of writing (50% off or $34.99, or $30.79 if you have BL2 already through the Borderlands² Bundle) and you'd have plenty of fun with it with likely a lot of content in that open world even if it feels a little one-note. I wouldn't recommend buying it at full price though so long as it uses Denuvo, and so long as performance remains this poor especially if you have a weaker GPU. Either get it half-off or wait for a steeper sale. I'm so torn because the open world and performance is trying its hardest to bring the game down, but for the price of "free" I absolutely loved my time with the game and I'm going to miss it when the weekend ends.

I got to spend a little while with the game during the free-to-play weekend, and my biggest takeaway is pretty simple: it actually feels like Borderlands.

Ok, I managed to beat the story, not including any side quests (except for 1), within about 15 hours during a free weekend.

First off, let me say the gunplay, movement, and controls are tight and refined to a T. It had me in a flow state during gunfights and bosses. The way I was playing involved a lot of dashing and weapon switching. In a way, it reminded me of Doom Eternal without the glory kills, which is a heavy compliment because that is the pinnacle of what I think an FPS should be: fast, responsive, and constant movement to stay alive. I have no complaints except there is an enemy modifier that sucks you into the center of where the enemy died, it is aids to deal with especially if there is multiple since you are forced to use both dashes to escape or go into FFYL/ take a chunk of damage.

The UI, in my opinion, is a downgrade from BL2 and BL3. They both kept it simple and clean without too many submenus to get lost in, but BL4 dropped the ball in this department. It has too many menus, which slowed down navigating your inventory, including selling and comparing. Also, for me, I missed being able to see the world from your inventory menu. It just looked much nicer to me, but that's my personal opinion.

Now, the story. I think it had better writing than 3 (low bar, I know). I found it somewhat enjoyable, but honestly, I was playing just to get to the end due to the free weekend, so I didn't really care what the characters were saying, and I just wanted to move on. The main villain is very threatening, albeit I feel like he is really dumb because he could've easily killed us. Now, performance. There's still A LOT to be desired from a game that looks like this. I only experienced a few bugs, with some doors not opening and me having to reload the game, along with some issues during the cutscenes, but overall, it didn't crash once.

[h1] Its fun. [/h1]  

There are a couple downsides, which I'll list in a second, but overall at 36 hours I have thoroughly enjoyed most of it.

[b]Upsides[/b]
* Good Story: Most of the flaws I've seen Youtubers complain about regarding the story were just from them not paying attention?(Or maybe a bug the game had at launch which cut some lines?).

* Best Mobility in the Series: Gliders act as a replacement For Oz Kits and That combined with Side dashes, Double jumps, Slides and grappling(where possible) Makes the traversal of areas the most fun in any BL game i have played.

* The Guns: This time around they are INCREDIBLE I've seen myself using Green to purple tier guns During my whole Playthrough, The License System makes For some extremely fun Synergies, for example a Gun with both Ripper and TORGUE becomes many times better gaining Full auto shooting.

* The Characters: At first I thought they looked really bland, But upon actually Playing Their Uniqueness becomes more apparent, In the way they talk, Act, Fight, etc...(C4SH and Loveless also add More Diversity in Appearance).

* Ordnances: Grenades No longer control your G(RB) Button With Rocket launchers having moved from a main gun to An Ordnance The addition of Miniguns and Knives, Variety is king here, On my main Character(Rafa) I found myself Using Them All at least Two or three times, Albeit i Liked Knife and Rocket launcher Ordnances more than any other.

* Encore: Best addition in the Game hands down, no more Savequit farming, No more having to run Through Five gauntlets of enemies to reach a boss area, Now you can just Refarm it Directly, 10/10 Feature, Please make a comeback in future entries.

* Contracts: Very Fun Tasks to do when exploring the open world, These help pass the time, and are a nice way to Avoid Infamy.



[b]The DOWN Sides *dun dun duuun*[/b]

* Infamy: This Feature hurts Replayability So much, Ever ask yourself that you would love to be forced into not playing the main story for 10-20 minutes at a crucial point that had you invested because enemies now heavily overpower you? me neither, This feature Has no meter, So you don't know how screwed you are or how many Sidequests are enough to make it go away, Is intrusive during gameplay and overall just Slows the games pace down, 0/10 Please dont ever bring this back EVER, I Truly dont think there is a way to make this work, Contracts are the only things that make this Bearable.

* Boss XP: Guys... Who ever complained about Boss XP gain being too high? Who?? Why Reduce it to barely above a normal enemy kill??? I legitimately have gained more XP killing the Adds to a Boss fight than the boss itself.

* NG+: Game doesn't Really have one, Heavily Hurts Replayability.

* Dialog Skipping: A feature that has been asked for in 3(BLTPS BL3 TTWL) Games STILL does not exist without mods, This game has the most Dialog in ANY Borderlands game with a lot of it slowing down Heavy action Missions to a Crawl, Maybe make it a feature for NG+? if one ever is added.

* Unique Items: Normal Unique items got removed in favour of having them all be legendary and that just makes some really lame legendaries exist, Could downgrade half of the legendaries i've used into normal Unique items and it'd make no difference, Their lack also hurts Side missions since there is no real reward after completing them once, So again, This hurts replayability.

* Open World: I'm mostly neutral towards this one, i just wish there were more Fast travel locations.


[b]Overall Score: 8/10[/b]

Could Be higher if the Fixable problems are... well.... Fixed, Especially Dialog Skipping.

Borderlands 4 — Review

Verdict: Not worth it, even at half off

Played through the free weekend and beat it. It's better than the movie. That's the nicest thing I have to say about it.

They took basically everything wonderful about the previous Borderlands games and slammed it into the side of a mountain.

Enemies & Combat

Bullet sponges, plain and simple. There's zero incentive to gear up because no matter what you're carrying, enemies just soak up damage. I started skipping entire crowds because fighting them was so repetitive and boring — not worth my time.

Enemy variety is basically nonexistent. It's one giant open world with no unique fauna to speak of. The strategy becomes: find a weapon that covers the elemental type you know is coming, and just carry it until something harder-hitting in the same flavor shows up. There's no real reason to experiment.

Bosses are more of the same — spongey, predictable, and easy to beat even when you're massively underleveled for them. No tension, no spectacle.

Guns & Loot

Had zero interest in the guns this time around, which is a first for this series. The three new manufacturers are a mixed bag:

Order — basically a fancier Jakobs. Hold to charge, tap to fire. Nothing new.
Ripper — actually interesting, the one bright spot.
Daedalus — the best of the three; lets you switch fire between different ammo types when you run out.
Skill Trees

This was a genuine highlight. Played Siren, and her take on a "hunter using necromancer powers" is a unique spin I hadn't seen before. That said, the pet aspect of the tree felt kind of samey compared to what's come before.

World Design & Terrain

The open world is a nice idea on paper, but the terrain is repetitive and boring — it all blurs together. And practically speaking, an open map doesn't suit Borderlands' structure well. Expect constant backtracking, rechecking locations, and getting lost.

Story & Writing

Boring, meandering, and never once grabbed my attention.

The humor fell flatter than paper — nothing landed a smile, a chuckle, or even a "hmm." For a series known for its irreverent tone, that's a real miss.

The callback/nostalgia beats are painfully telegraphed — you can see the "ooh, remember how shocking this was?? It's gonna happen again!!" moments coming from a mile away, and they just made me roll my eyes.

The surprise B-plot boss reveal itself was a genuine surprise, but the character's entire motivation boils down to misplaced blame — being furious at people for things they had no way of knowing, including someone who'd been trapped in hell for six years and still gets blamed. It reads less like compelling conflict and more like a character just looking for someone to be mad at.

Technical Performance

Frame lags constantly. Render/shader compile stutters on every single load-in — genuinely one of the more annoying technical issues I've dealt with in a recent release.

Small Wins

Returning characters got noticeably hotter hairstyles/redesigns this time around — a minor but appreciated detail.

Final Verdict

Not worth full price, not worth half off. If I were pricing it myself: maybe $20, preowned, from a discount bin or Goodwill. That's the ceiling.

PROS:
+ cool mobility: grappling hook, dashes, gliding, double jump, and overall verticality (kind of like doom eternal).
+ gunplay and visuals: the graphics look a little better now, and the impact from guns feels way more enjoyable.
+ progression & classes: 4 base characters + 2 DLC ones; overall they feel familiar if you've played the other borderlands games. i ran with Vex, who has multiple subclasses that give some build flexibility, though it would be cool if we could combine them, imo.
+ open world: a bit of a double-edged sword, as it feels a little stretched out.
+ story: its fine, with no cringe
+ loot & content: a lot of stuff to do and almost zero loading screens between zones. the variety of items is crazy; drop rates for legendary guns are lower than in BD3, but blue or purple guns can actually be good, so it's not just a mind-numbing legendary reroll farm.

THE BIGGEST CON IS OPTIMIZATION:
this game constantly experiences frame drops at random moments (btw it compiles shaders on launch, in main menu, in the settings and then while you're just running around or fast-traveling (200gb yes)), along with crashes and freezes. without frame generation, you won't even get 120 FPS on medium or low settings, even though the graphics aren't exactly mind-blowing.

OVERALL
gameplay and gunplay-wise, this is easily the best entry in the series if you ignore the performance issues. its  definitely worth buying if you have a high-end PC, but it sucks seeing devs completely stop giving a damn about optimization. if your pc cant handle it, just play BD3 it's honestly just as good
